columns.name: famaekvivadisp_13
columns.label: Household-equivalised disposable income
columns.note: This is the family's disposable income divided by an equivalence factor, so that families of different sizes can be compared. The factor counts the first adult as 1.0, each further person over 14 as 0.5, and each child under 15 as 0.3: a couple with two young children comes to 1 + 0.5 + 0.6 = 2.1, so a family income of 420,000 is recorded as 200,000 for each of the four. `FAMDISPONIBEL_13` is the same money before that division, and `FAMAEKVIVAINDKNETTO` is a different income concept (total income with net interest), so check which one your analysis plan means. The `_13` suffix marks the definition that replaced the older variables from 2013: DST states that FAMDISPONIBEL was discontinued in 2013 and replaced by FAMDISPONIBEL_13. A study spanning 2013 has to know which side of that change it is on. DST's year ranges settle the relationship with the sister column FAMAEKVIVADISP, which has no _13: the old one runs 1990-2012, this one runs 1987-2024. The _13 definition was applied backwards as well as forwards, so it is not a newer variable covering later years only. A study spanning the 2013 changeover should use _13 for the whole period rather than splicing the two, which would mix two definitions in one series.
columns.derivation: FAMAEKVIVADISP_13 = FAMDISPONIBEL_13 / (1 + (0.5 * (number of people over 14 in the family - 1)) + (0.3 * number of people under 15 in the family))

columns.name: patient_cpr
columns.label: Personal identifier
columns.note: Results carrying only a replacement CPR number are filtered out before the research table is built, so every row here has a real personal identifier. The narrower `laboratorieproevesvar` table calls this column `cprnummer`.

columns.name: samplingdate
columns.label: Sampling date
columns.note: When the sample was taken, not when the result was reported. This guide previously called the column `samplingdato`, which does not exist.

columns.name: samplingtime
columns.label: Sampling time
columns.note: Not in the narrower `lab_forsker` table.

columns.name: analysiscode
columns.label: Analyte code
columns.note: Which analysis was done, coded in NPU or the Danish DNK terminology. This is the column the guide used to call `npu`, which does not exist. Only NPU- and DNK-coded results reach the research table, about 95 per cent of all results: anything coded with a laboratory's own local code is absent.

columns.name: value
columns.label: Result
columns.note: Text, not a number. Alongside numeric results the table holds a fixed set of words: POSITIV, NEGATIV, NORMAL, IKKE PAAVIST, PAAVIST, INGEN VAEKST, FORHOEJET and the blood-type codes. as.numeric() turns every one of those into NA without warning, which drops exactly the samples where something was found. The narrower `laboratorieproevesvar` table calls this column `samplevalue`.

columns.name: unit
columns.label: Unit
columns.note: Never compare values across laboratories without checking this. Different equipment and sample material mean the same analyte code can need different interpretation, within one laboratory over time as well.

columns.name: resulttype
columns.label: Result type
columns.note: Whether the result is numeric or alphanumeric. Use it to split the two before converting anything.

columns.name: laboratorium_idcode
columns.label: Laboratory identifier
columns.note: A MedCom laboratory code. Coverage starts at different dates per laboratory, so this column is what tells you whether a gap in a series is clinical or administrative.

columns.name: resultvalidation
columns.label: Result validation
columns.note: Not in the narrower `lab_forsker` table.

columns.name: operator
columns.label: Operator
columns.note: Carries the "less than" or "greater than" sign when a result is reported as below or above a detection limit. Ignoring it turns a censored value into an exact one.

columns.name: pnr
columns.label: Personal identifier
columns.note: DST's variable list calls this column `PNR12`. Check whether your variable is named `pnr` or `pnr12`.

columns.name: eksd
columns.label: Dispensing date
columns.note: The date the prescription was collected at the pharmacy. Not the date it was prescribed, and not evidence that the medicine was taken.

columns.name: vnr
columns.label: Item number (product key)
columns.note: The only reliable way to isolate one specific product. Two brands with the same active substance share an ATC code but have different item numbers.

columns.name: indo

columns.label: CPR_BARN
columns.note: The child's CPR number, which is how the register joins to every other register about the child.

columns.name: cpr_moder
columns.label: CPR_MODER
columns.note: The mother's CPR number. There is a row per child, so a mother of three appears three times.

columns.name: gestationsalder_dage
columns.label: GESTATIONSALDER_DAGE
columns.note: Gestational age in days, not weeks. Divide by 7 for the usual clinical scale.

columns.name: paritet
columns.label: PARITET
columns.note: Parity. Counts previous births, so it is not the same as the number of children currently alive.

columns.name: ydernr
columns.label: Provider number
columns.note: A provider number, not a person. DST's variable list does not say what unit it identifies or whether it is stable when a practice changes hands, so do not use it to follow an individual clinician over time without checking that first.

columns.name: speciale
columns.label: Specialty, 6-digit
columns.note: The 6-digit specialty code is what distinguishes a GP contact from a specialist one. There is no separate contact-type column: the specialty is the classification.

columns.name: ydlant
columns.label: Number of services under the specialty
columns.note: One row can cover several services, so counting rows undercounts activity. Sum this column instead.

columns.name: afrper
columns.label: Settlement period
columns.note: DST labels this "Afregningsperiode", a settlement period rather than a treatment date. Nothing in the variable list says how far settlement can lag the contact, so check the distribution against honuge before using it as a date.

columns.name: sikgrup
columns.label: Insurance group
columns.note: Group 1 patients need a referral from their GP to see a specialist, physiotherapist, chiropodist or psychologist, and pay nothing. Group 2 patients may go directly to any GP or specialist, but pay the difference between the fee and the regional subsidy themselves. The two groups therefore leave different traces for the same clinical need, so group membership is a confounder in any analysis of specialist use. Source: borger.dk, "Sygesikring og sikringsgrupper".

columns.name: kontakt
columns.label: Contact
columns.note: Not in SYSI. Do not assume a comparable count of contacts before 2005.

columns.name: koenimp
columns.label: Sex, imputed values included
columns.note: Imputed where the source was missing, so it is not identical to koen in BEF. Prefer BEF when you need sex as a study variable.

columns.name: year
columns.label: Register year
columns.note: Not a DST variable. It is the partition the yearly deliveries were written into, so filtering on it stops the other years being read at all. Use it to limit how much is read, not to decide when something happened: for that, use the register's own date column.
columns.origin: not a DST variable - added by parquet conversion

columns.name: pnr
columns.label: Personal identifier
columns.note: DST's variable list calls this column PNR. Some deliveries rename it: some deliveries hand it over as `v_cpr`. The name is a product of the data processing, not of the register, so check your own columns and rename.

columns.name: recnum
columns.label: Contact identifier
columns.note: DST's variable list calls this column RECNUM, the same name the somatic lpr_adm uses. Some deliveries rename it, and not consistently: the contact table can arrive as `k_recnum` and the diagnosis table as `v_recnum`. Rename both to recnum before joining.

columns.name: c_pattype
columns.label: Contact type
columns.note: Present here even where the somatic lpr_adm extract leaves it out, so the psychiatric side of a study can be classified when the somatic side cannot. Do not assume symmetry between the two extracts.

columns.name: d_ebhdto
columns.label: Data for endelig behandling (Variabel udgået efter 31.12.2003)

columns.name: d_opdatdto
columns.label: Intern dato for opdatering af kontakten

columns.name: v_alddg
columns.label: Alder i dage ved kontaktens start

columns.name: v_alder
columns.label: Alder i år ved kontaktens start

columns.name: v_aldmdr
columns.label: Alder i måneder ved kontaktens start

columns.name: recnum
columns.label: Contact identifier
columns.note: DST's variable list calls this column RECNUM. Some deliveries rename it, and not consistently: this table can arrive as `v_recnum` while the contact table gets `k_recnum`. One key, three names. Check and rename to recnum.

columns.name: hfaudd
columns.label: Highest completed education
columns.note: A code for which education, not for its level. UDDA carries no level column at all, so the level has to come from a lookup table.

columns.name: udd
columns.label: Education code
columns.note: Not the same code system as hfaudd. Under DISCED-15, AUDD codes describe a completed education and UDD codes one that is ongoing or was interrupted, so a lookup table built for one will not fit the other.

columns.name: hfinstnr
columns.label: Institution that awarded the education
columns.note: The guide previously referred to this column as `INSTNR`. DST's list has no INSTNR; the institution columns are HFINSTNR, ALMINSTNR, ERHINSTNR and IGINSTNR, one per kind of education.

columns.name: almaudd
columns.label: Highest completed general education
columns.note: The general-education track only. hfaudd is the highest completed education of any kind, so the two answer different questions and are not interchangeable.

columns.name: alm_vfra
columns.label: Date the general education was obtained

columns.name: erh_vfra
columns.label: Date the vocational education was obtained

columns.name: ig_vfra
columns.label: Start date of the ongoing education
columns.note: Pairs with udd: this is when the ongoing education began. An education with a start and no completion is either still running or was interrupted, and the register does not distinguish the two.

atc.name: ATC (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical)
atc.description: The WHO classification of medicines. Five cumulative levels: 1 character (anatomical main group), 3 (therapeutic subgroup), 4 (pharmacological subgroup), 5 (chemical subgroup), 7 (chemical substance). Each level repeats the levels above it and adds characters, so C09AA05 contains C, C09, C09A and C09AA.
atc.note: As a rule, filter on the full 7-character code rather than on the level columns: `atc2` holds three characters, so a longer pattern matched against it can never match, and it returns nothing at all with no error. The level columns are well suited to grouping, and to filtering when every code you want is the same length as the column.

civst.name: Civilstand (marital status)
civst.description: Marital status in the CPR data behind BEF. Single-letter codes.
civst.note: Codes P, O and L came in with the registered-partnership act of 1 October 1989; before that the set was smaller. Registered partnerships could no longer be entered into from 15 June 2012.

diagtype.name: Diagnosetype (LPR2 c_diagtype)
diagtype.description: Whether a diagnosis is the reason for the contact, an additional condition, or something else. Six codes, three of which were discontinued.
diagtype.note: The guide long described this as an A/B/G column. There are six codes, and three of them stop: **G runs 1995-2003 only**, M 1998-2013 and C 2002-2013. A and B run the whole period, H from 1995. So a comorbidity definition built on G silently covers nine years and nothing else, and filtering to A/B/G drops referral diagnoses entirely. Which types to keep is a case definition, not a technicality: outcomes usually use A and B. Carry the type column into the extract so the definition can be varied later.

values.en: Action diagnosis - the reason for the contact
Underlying condition, where different from the action diagnosis
Provisional diagnosis, open somatic outpatient visits only
values.da: Midlertidig diagnose, kun for aabne somatisk ambulante besoeg

hfaudd.name: DISCED-15 AUDD (completed education)
hfaudd.description: The code for a completed education under DISCED-15. Four digits identifying which education, not how long or how high it is. DISCED-15 has a separate code for an ongoing or interrupted education (UDD).
hfaudd.note: This is an identifier, not a scale. The level (short, medium, long) has to be looked up in a separate table, and cannot be read off the digits: 4112 is an electrician, and taking the first two digits as a level code makes it a long higher education. DST documents the ongoing-education codes separately as DISCED-15 UDD.

icd10.name: ICD-10 (Danish edition)
icd10.description: Diagnosis codes. The Danish edition prefixes the WHO code with the letter D, so WHO's E11 appears as DE11 in LPR.
icd10.note: The D prefix is a Danish addition, not part of the WHO code. Matching WHO codes directly against LPR without allowing for it returns nothing.

indm.name: Indlaeggelsesmaade (LPR2 c_indm)
indm.description: Whether the contact was acute or planned. Three codes, one of which was discontinued.
indm.note: From 2014 this is what separates an emergency-room visit from an ordinary outpatient one, because `c_pattype` code `3` was discontinued and both arrive as `2`. Code `9` (Uoplyst) stops at the end of 2003, so a missing value after that is genuinely missing rather than coded as unknown.

indud_kode.name: Indud_kode (migration direction)
indud_kode.description: Whether a migration event is an immigration or an emigration.
indud_kode.note: Use `U` for censoring at emigration. People who never emigrated have no `U` event at all, so they are simply absent rather than carrying a missing date. Two caveats from the guide: CPR only has complete immigration and emigration data from 1971, so someone who immigrated before that has no event and looks resident since birth; and a move to Greenland is a status of its own in CPR rather than an emigration. Confirm the values on your own delivery.

koen.name: Køn (sex)
koen.description: Sex as coded in BEF. Small enumerated set.

kom.name: Kommunekode (municipality code)
kom.description: Municipality of residence. Three-digit codes. 98 municipalities since the 2007 reform, which replaced the previous 271. Christiansø (411) is not under a municipality but administered directly by the state.
kom.note: These codes are valid from 1 January 2007. A study reaching further back needs the pre-reform classification, where the same number can mean a different municipality.

kont_type.name: Contact type (LPR3 kont_type)
kont_type.description: The LPR3 contact type. Coded in SKS rather than as single digits, so the values look nothing like LPR2's c_pattype and cannot be mapped across one to one.
kont_type.note: `ALCA00` means physical attendance, which is the closest LPR3 gets to LPR2's inpatient flag. It marks attendance, not admission, so a study that treats it as "was admitted" will include outpatient visits.

oprart.name: Procedureart (LPR2 c_oprart)
oprart.description: What role a procedure code plays on the contact: the main one, a sub-procedure or an add-on code.
oprart.note: Counting rows in the procedure table counts add-on codes and sub-procedures as procedures. If you want one row per operation, filter to `V` or `P` first. All four codes run from 1996 with no breaks.

values.en: Main procedure of the completed contact

pattype.name: Patienttype (LPR2 c_pattype)
pattype.description: The patient's administrative relationship to the hospital. LPR2 only: LPR3 has no equivalent, and the type has to be derived from contact duration plus an acute marker.
pattype.note: There are four codes, not six, and they changed meaning. Code `1` was Dagpatient until 1986 and Deldoegnspatient from 1987; code `2` was Natpatient until 1986 and Ambulant from 1987. The register only started using `1`, `2` and `3` in 1994, so before that essentially every contact is `0`. Code `3` was discontinued at the end of 2013, and from 2014 an emergency-room visit arrives as `2` with an acute admission mode in `c_indm`. Reading `2` as outpatient across the whole register therefore mislabels night patients before 1987 and emergency visits after 2013.

reg.name: Region
reg.description: Region of residence. The five regions created by the 2007 municipal reform, plus a code for unknown.
reg.note: Do not confuse these with AMT, the pre-2007 counties, which has 16 codes in the ranges 11-14, 21-24, 31-37 and 88. Different geography, different era.

sex_lpr.name: Koen in LPR2 (c_sex)
sex_lpr.description: Sex as recorded on a hospital contact. Not the same coding as BEF's `koen`, and not the same coding across the register's own lifetime.
sex_lpr.note: The coding changed at the start of 2005: `1`/`2` until the end of 2004, `M`/`K` from 2005. A study spanning that year that filters on `c_sex == "2"` keeps only the women seen before 2005 and silently drops the rest, with no error and no empty result to warn you. Take sex from BEF instead, where it is `koen` coded `1`/`2` throughout, unless you specifically need what the hospital recorded.

sks.name: SKS procedure codes
sks.description: Sundhedsvaesenets Klassifikations System. The procedure branch of the same classification that supplies diagnosis codes, used in LPR_SKSOPR and LPR_SKSUBE. Surgical procedures sit under K, examinations and other non-surgical procedures under the remaining letters.
sks.note: The codes are hierarchical, so a prefix match selects a whole branch. That also makes it easy to select more than you meant: check how many characters your intended group actually needs before filtering with starts_with().

socio13.name: Socioøkonomisk klassifikation, version 2013
socio13.description: Socioeconomic classification: employment status, self-employment, students, pensioners, people outside the labour market.
socio13.note: DST publishes four versions for different eras (SOCIO_GL, SOCIO, SOCIO02, SOCIO13). They are not interchangeable, so a study spanning the boundaries has to decide which one it uses and check that it covers the whole period.

akm.name: Arbejdsklassifikationsmodulet (labour classification module)
akm.description: One record per person per year with their socioeconomic classification: employed, self-employed, student, unemployed, pensioner, outside the labour market.

bef.name: Befolkningen (population register)
bef.description: Status register with one snapshot per person per reference time point. Delivered quarterly since 2008 (March, June, September, December); December only before that, so the cadence is not constant across the coverage.

cancer.name: Cancerregisteret
cancer.description: One row per incident cancer diagnosis: a person appears once per tumour, not once in total. Running since 1943, which makes it one of the longest continuous cancer registries in the world.

dod.name: Døde i Danmark (deaths in Denmark)
dod.description: One row per deceased person. This is the register to use for date of death, and it covers the whole period on its own.

dodsaars.name: Dødsårssagsregistret
dodsaars.description: Cause of death for 1970-2001. Closed. It also carries a date of death, which is why it is so often used for censoring, but that use is a mistake for any study running past 2001.

dodsaarsager.name: Dødsårsagsregister (2022-)
dodsaarsager.description: Cause of death from 2022. The current register, and the third naming scheme the chain has used.

dodsaasg.name: Dødsårsagsregister (2002-2022)
dodsaasg.description: Cause of death for 2002-2022. Closed. Takes over from DODSAARS and is itself replaced by DODSAARSAGER.

faik.name: Familieindkomster (family income)
faik.description: Household income per year, keyed on the household rather than the person. Reaching it from a person means going through BEF for the familie_id.

lab_dm_forsker.name: Laboratoriedatabasens Forskertabel
lab_dm_forsker.description: One row per laboratory result attached to a request: a blood or other sample, its analyte code, the result and its unit. Very large - well over a billion rows - so filter before collecting.

lmdb.name: Lægemiddeldatabasen (prescription register)
lmdb.description: One row per dispensed prescription, so the same person appears many times. Covers prescriptions dispensed at community pharmacies.

lpr_a_diagnose.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - diagnoseoplysning
lpr_a_diagnose.description: One row per diagnosis on a contact. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_a_kontakt on dw_ek_kontakt to reach the person.

lpr_a_kontakt.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - kontaktoplysninger
lpr_a_kontakt.description: One row per hospital contact. Carries pnr, so the diagnosis and procedure tables reach the person through it. DST gives the coverage as 2017-2025: the table reaches back before the March 2019 LPR3 boundary because outpatient contacts already held in LPR2 were folded into it.

lpr_a_procregistrering.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - procedureregistreringer
lpr_a_procregistrering.description: One row per procedure registration. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_a_kontakt on dw_ek_kontakt, exactly as the diagnosis table does.

lpr_adm.name: Landspatientregistret - administrative oplysninger
lpr_adm.description: One row per hospital contact. This is the only LPR2 dataset that carries pnr, so every other one reaches the person through it.

lpr_diag.name: Landspatientregistret - diagnoser
lpr_diag.description: One row per diagnosis on a contact, so a contact can have several. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.

lpr_sksopr.name: Landspatientregistret - operationer
lpr_sksopr.description: One row per surgical procedure. Carries no pnr and no admission date: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.

lpr_sksube.name: Landspatientregistret - undersoegelser og behandlinger
lpr_sksube.description: One row per examination or treatment. Structured exactly like LPR_SKSOPR, and joined to lpr_adm on recnum in the same way.

mfr.name: Det Medicinske Foedselsregister
mfr.description: One row per birth, carrying both the mother and the child. A mother appears once per birth, so the register is keyed on the child rather than the person.

sssy.name: Sygesikring (6-cifret)
sssy.description: The continuation of SYSI: fees settled for primary-care activity. Same shape, a few different columns. Both registers report 2005, so a study spanning the handover has to pick one source for that year or it will double-count.

sysi.name: Sygesikring (6-cifret)
sysi.description: Fees settled for primary-care activity: general practice, practising specialists, dentists, physiotherapists and so on. One row per settled service group, not one row per visit.

t_psyk_adm.name: Landspatientregistret psykiatri - administrative oplysninger
t_psyk_adm.description: One row per psychiatric hospital contact, up to March 2019. The psychiatric counterpart of lpr_adm, and separate from it: a study covering both somatic and psychiatric care has to read both registers and stack them.

t_psyk_diag.name: Landspatientregistret psykiatri - diagnoser
t_psyk_diag.description: One row per diagnosis on a psychiatric contact. Carries no person identifier: join to t_psyk_adm to reach the person.

udda.name: Uddannelser (BUE) (education register)
udda.description: One record per person per year, updated when the education changes. Holds the code for the education a person completed, not its level.

vnds.name: Historiske vandringer (historical migrations)
vnds.description: One row per migration event per person: an immigration to or an emigration from Denmark, with the date it happened. Holds only events, so a person born in Denmark who never left has no rows at all - absence is the normal case, not missing data. Known to contain duplicates, which is why DST replaced it. Closed by DST and replaced by three registers: VNDS_IND and VNDS_UD from 2005, and VNDS_HIST for 1973-2004. VNDS itself runs to 2024, so its coverage overlaps both successors for 2005-2024. Closed by DST in February 2026 and split into VNDS_IND, VNDS_UD and VNDS_HIST. Still documented as a current register because deliveries made before the split contain only this one, which is the case for many projects.
vnds.overlap_note: Coverage overlaps the successors for 2005-2024, but they must not be combined. DST states that migration data over the years came from different sources and that this produced a number of duplicates, and that freezing the earliest data in a historical register reduces the problem. The three successors are therefore a correction of this register, not a reorganisation of it. Use either VNDS on its own, accepting the duplicates it is known to contain, or VNDS_HIST together with VNDS_IND and VNDS_UD - never a mixture.

vnds_hist.name: Historiske vandringer fra 1973 til 2004
vnds_hist.description: One row per migration event per person for 1973-2004. Frozen: DST marks it as closed, and it is not updated.

vnds_ind.name: Indvandringer (immigrations)
vnds_ind.description: One row per immigration from 2005 onwards, with the person's demographics as at the event.

vnds_ud.name: Udvandringer (emigrations)
vnds_ud.description: One row per emigration from 2005 onwards, with the person's demographics as at the event.
